headline: The night brought mildly good news: oil fell about 1.8% and US futures are up, so Nifty looks set to open around 100 points higher. The real test is whether Friday's bounce can hold while foreign funds keep selling.

mood.label: Mixed
mood.why: The dashboard scores −15 on a −100 to +100 scale (neutral), with only 2 of 4 checks agreeing. Data built 08:47 IST, overnight data as of 08:48 IST.

key_points.text: Brent crude fell **1.8%** to about $103 on Russia-Ukraine truce hopes. India imports most of its oil, so this helps.
GIFT Nifty was near 22,625 around 8 am, about 100 points above Nifty's Friday close of 22,520, and US futures are up 0.3%.
My call: a small follow-through on Friday's 1.3% bounce, with low confidence. Sellers wait near 23,000.
India inflation data at 4 pm, five days after RBI raised rates to 5.50%.

sections.title: What changed overnight
sections.summary: Mostly better news for India, supporting Friday's bounce; Korea is the weak spot.

points.text: US stocks rose 0.6% on Friday and US futures are up another **0.3%** this morning.
Brent is down **1.8%** at $102.8 on the truce news, which neither Russia nor Ukraine has confirmed. Tanker attacks near Hormuz keep it above $100.
Asia is mixed: Korea's Kospi is down **2.5%**, Hong Kong is up 0.3% and China is flat. Japan is closed for a holiday.
The dollar is flat and US bond markets are shut for a holiday. Infosys, Wipro and HDFC Bank shares in the US rose 0.3–1.8% on Friday.

sections.title: Bounce or continuation?
sections.summary: After Friday's 1.3% jump off a multi-month low, I lean to mild follow-through, low confidence.

points.text: For more bounce: oil falling, US futures up, India VIX (the fear gauge) down from 15.3 to 14.4.
Only **9.6%** of FII index-futures bets are on a rise, up from 8.5%. Below 10%, bets on a fall can be closed in a hurry, which lifts prices.
For a fade: the trend is still down and FIIs are still selling shares every day.
Proof I'm wrong: Nifty falling back below **22,500**, or below Thursday's 22,232.

sections.title: The big picture
sections.summary: The trend is still down, but the bets in options and futures no longer point clearly lower.

points.text: Price trend scores the worst possible **−2**: Nifty is below its 20, 50 and 200-day averages (22,972, 23,726, 24,266), with lower highs and lows.
Put-call ratio (bets on a fall compared with bets on a rise) jumped from 0.77 to **1.14** in five sessions; option sellers moved their floor up from 22,000 to 22,500.
Overall bias **−15** (neutral), 2 of 4 checks agree. VIX at 14.4 is middling, 70th percentile of the year.

sections.title: What big investors are doing
sections.summary: Foreign funds keep selling, Indian funds keep buying more, and foreign futures bets are slightly less negative.

points.text: FIIs sold ₹3,569 crore on Friday after a huge **₹12,944 crore** on Thursday; ₹25,595 crore in October so far.
Indian funds (DIIs) bought ₹4,743 crore on Friday, more than FIIs sold, and **₹25,132 crore** this month.
FIIs trimmed futures bets on a fall by 13,121 contracts, but still hold about **2.94 lakh** more bets on a fall than a rise.

sections.title: What the world is telling India
sections.summary: Outside India the picture is still a headwind, mainly from high US interest rates and dear oil.

points.text: Dashboard macro view: **Headwinds** (4 of 10 items hurt, 2 help); oil is still up 21% in three months.
US 6-month bills pay 4.32% vs the Fed's 3.88%, so markets expect a **Fed hike**, which pulls money from India.
The rupee is weak at 96.76 per dollar; the US 10-year rate is very high at **5.24%**.

sections.title: Company results
sections.summary: Results season has started reasonably well, led by TCS.

points.text: TCS: profit +14.9%, revenue +11.2% from last year, slightly above estimates. The stock rose **5.5%** Friday because hopes were low.
DMart: revenue +17.8%, profit +8.5%, in line. I couldn't confirm the market reaction.
HCL Tech reports after the close today, a test of whether IT relief spreads.

sections.title: What could change the picture
sections.summary: A busy two weeks: inflation in India and the US, bank results, and the Fed.

points.text: Wed 14 Oct: US inflation, expected up to **3.6%** from 3.4%. Higher would firm up Fed hike bets.
Fri 17 Oct: HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank and Axis Bank results; banks are Nifty's biggest part.
Holiday 20 Oct, Infosys 23 Oct, monthly expiry 27 Oct, Fed decision early 29 Oct.
Oil back above $105, or the truce collapsing, would undo today's good news.

levels.note: A close above 23,000 would also put Nifty above its 20-day average and break the run of lower highs; a close below 22,500 would mean put sellers have given up and the bounce has failed.

watch.text: Does Nifty hold a higher open near 22,600?
India CPI. Above August's 4.82% would hurt banks.
HCL Tech results after the close.
Weekly expiry tomorrow; moves near 22,500 and 23,000 can be sharp.

bottom_line: Cheaper oil, firmer US futures and GIFT Nifty about 100 points higher point to a positive start. But the dashboard is only neutral (−15, 2 of 4 checks agree): the trend is down, FIIs keep selling, and US rates and the rupee still work against India. My read is a mild follow-through toward 22,700–23,000, with low confidence. Main risks: today's inflation number and oil rebounding.
